# LeisureLinux Readings

> Reading notes, book reviews, and reflective commentary on technology, management, business, and the humanities. Written by LeisureLinux (Albert Xu) — a Linux kernel and infrastructure architect who has been an engineer and manager for over 30 years.

## About

LeisureLinux Readings is the reading-notebook companion to the main technical blog at freelamp.com. Every note distills a book's structure, core arguments, and practical takeaways, and adds the author's own critical perspective rather than mere summarizing. Topics span engineering, IT operations, organization design, management, business strategy, and personal effectiveness.

All content is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

## Reading Notes

<!-- New notes are appended here as they are published -->

## How Notes Are Written

- Pick books that can change a decision or an action.
- Read for the argument's logic, not just its conclusions.
- Structure each note around: what the book says → why it matters → what you can do differently.
- Write for a reader who has not read the book, so each note stands alone.
